subject: Private observability: SIEM forwarding, retention & tracing hooks
messages:
From: David Chapman <dchapman@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observability for private deployment: Splunk forwarding & retention

Rishi,

We're moving forward with a private VPC deployment for our pilot and security has a few specific asks around how logs/metrics/traces will be exported out of the private environment. Can you confirm the options Redwood supports and any constraints? Key questions below:

- We need to forward audit logs and scheduler/serving logs into our Splunk HEC or via TLS syslog. Do you support HEC or syslog over TLS natively, or do you expect a partner forwarder?
- If we push to S3 and ingest from our side, what networking patterns do you support for private transfer (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs SFTP)? Any recommendations for keeping data encrypted in transit and at rest?
- Retention: we need knobs to control retention windows per log type (audit vs request logs vs metrics). Can you scope retention controls & deletion workflows?
- Traces: we want to sample at 10% for production and keep full traces for errors. Can Redwood emit OTLP spans (collector) or do we need to run our own OpenTelemetry collector?
- PII: are there recommended filters to remove sensitive fields before export?

We are starting procurement next week and need these details for our SOC 2 assessment. CC'ing our Splunk integration engineer.

Thanks,
David Chapman
InfoSec Lead, Acme Corp


From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: David Chapman <dchapman@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Splunk Integration <splunk-int@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability for private deployment: Splunk forwarding & retention

Hi David — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by recommended patterns and next steps.

Short answers:
- HEC/syslog: Redwood Private can stream logs to an on-prem forwarder or directly to a customer HEC endpoint over mTLS/TLS. We also support syslog-ng compatible syslog over TLS.
- S3 export: yes — periodic exporting of structured logs/metrics to a customer-owned S3 bucket is supported; recommended transport is VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) with bucket-level KMS and an IAM role for ingestion.
- Retention: Redwood exposes retention policies per-log-class (audit, request, metrics) in the private config; deletion jobs can be scheduled and audited.
- Traces: Redwood can emit OTLP to an OpenTelemetry collector. For strict network isolation customers often run the OTEL collector in the same VPC and push to their backend via a private endpoint.
- PII filtering: we provide a filtering hook (configurable) that runs before export; common patterns: redaction by field, hashing of identifiers, or dropping request bodies for specific endpoints.

Recommended pattern (for Acme):
1) Primary export: TLS HEC endpoint from a small, hardened forwarder (filebeat/td-agent) inside the private VPC. Use mTLS; Redwood will sign requests with a client cert we provide for the deployment.
2) Secondary archive: daily S3 export encrypted with your KMS key via PrivateLink for longer-term retention and audit.
3) Traces: run OTEL collector in the VPC; Redwood will emit OTLP (TLS) to collector. Collector is responsible for sampling rules — we can ship a starter config that implements 10% default and 100% on error.
4) Retention controls: we will surface policy by log class in the deployment console and provide a delete workflow with an audit log that you can ship to Splunk.

I'll attach our playbook and checklist; Hannah and Markus on my team will propose minimal config snippets for filebeat and OTEL and a retention matrix. Can we schedule a 30-minute runbook review on Tuesday 2/17 or Wednesday 2/18?

Next steps:
- I will circulate the playbook and a minimal OTEL config.
- Hannah to draft the forwarded-configs. Markus to confirm KMS flow and audit log reencryption.

Attachments: rwinf_siem_playbook_v1.pdf; deployment-ops-checklist.csv

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference


From: David Chapman <dchapman@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: Observability for private deployment: SIEM forwarding & retention

Rishi — that sounds good. We prefer Primary export via HEC (mTLS) plus S3 archive via PrivateLink. A few clarifications from our compliance team:

- Retention controls: can you confirm retention can be set independently by log class and that deletion will emit an auditable event with timestamp and operator id?
- KMS: we need to use our customer-managed key (CMK) for S3 server-side encryption and manage key rotation — will Redwood accept a KMS grant approach?
- PII filters: do you have built-in JSON field selectors or is it regex-based? We need deterministic removal (not just masking).

If you can confirm those, we can mark the security checklist as green and move forward with procurement.

Thanks,
David
